data.cultural_impact: The name Altayyib holds a deep cultural significance for Muslims as it is a constant reminder of the importance of moral values and purity in the Islamic faith. In Islamic societies and communities, the name is often given to newborns as a reflection of the parents’ hope for their child to grow up to be a virtuous and pure individual. It also serves as an inspiration for children, motivating them to live up to the name and strive towards purifying their souls and actions throughout their lives.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Altayyib holds tremendous significance as it is a reminder for Muslims to constantly work towards achieving purity in both their inner and outer lives. It is a reflection of the belief that a truly devoted Muslim strives to purify their soul from worldly desires and the impurities of sin by following the teachings of Allah and His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). By living a virtuous life that is guided by moral values and away from sin, an individual achieves a state of ultimate spiritual fulfillment and comes closer to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah. The life of Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf as-Sufyani (d. 658 AD). Al-Hajjaj was given the honorific name 'Altayyib' meaning 'the good' by Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz.
historical_references.context: Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz, the Umayyad caliph, bestowed the name 'Altayyib' ('the good') upon Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf as a mark of respect and admiration for his piety and leadership qualities.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam's Futuh Misr. Description of the invasion of Egypt by the Caliph Omar ibn Al-Khattab (640 AD). Al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad was a leader of the Egyptian resistance during the Muslim invasion. He was killed and his head was presented to Caliph Omar. Caliph Omar ordered that his head be buried under the name 'Altayyib' meaning 'the good'.
historical_references.context: Caliph Omar ibn Al-Khattab ordered the burial of Al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad's head under the name 'Altayyib' as a mark of respect and acknowledgement of his bravery and leadership during the resistance against the Muslim invasion.
